3: One does not place an animal in the inns of idolaters, and one does not hand over an animal to their shepherd, because they are suspected of bestiality; and in places where they are not suspected of this, and on the contrary they strike and punish for it, it is permitted.
A Jew shall not seclude himself with idolaters, because they are suspected of bloodshed.

If an idolater happens to meet him on the road, girded with a sword, he should place him on his right
(the same applies to an idolater with a staff in his hand—he should place him on his left) (Tur).
If they were ascending on an ascent or descending on a descent, the Jew should not be below and the idolater above
(and nevertheless he should place him somewhat to his right) (Ran, chapter Ein Ma‘amidin).
And he should never bow before him.
If he asks him, “Where are you going?”—if he needs to go one parasang, he should say, “I am going two parasangs.”
A Jewish woman shall not seclude herself with an idolater, even if they are many and their wives are with them.
